item.title: Stephen A. Smith Says Phone Was Banned As Backlash Over Dinner With Trump Continues
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Stephen A. Smith cited a White House phone ban after Charlamagne Tha God called for a public record of his Trump dinner.
item.content:encoded:
Stephen A. Smith said he had to put his phone away before his dinner with Donald Trump. That was his answer to Charlamagne Tha God’s call for a public record of the White House visit.

The ESPN host addressed the point on “Straight Shooter” on October 20. He said he learned about the phone rule at the gate and handed his phone to his bodyguard.

“Would you have preferred that I turned around and not attend the meeting?” Smith asked.

For Charlamagne, the issue was who got to shape the story after dinner. On “The Breakfast Club”, he argued that media figures should speak with Trump on the record. That way, viewers could judge the exchange for themselves.

He wasn’t against the meeting itself. He wanted to see the guests press Trump, not just hear their accounts later. With no record to watch, he said, people were left to ask why the guests went and what they hoped to gain.

“I don’t want to just hear it from you after the fact. I want to see it,” he said.

Smith said Bill Maher, Maher’s executive producer and Kid Rock also had to give up their phones.

He said he respected Charlamagne and “The Breakfast Club” and had called him before the visit. He didn’t view their critique as a personal attack. Smith said he, too, would have liked to record the exchange.

The two had spoken about Trump before. In March 2024, Smith told Charlamagne he wouldn’t vote for Trump due to his conduct. That was more than two years before the dinner.

The visit took place on October 15. On CNN the next night, Smith said he went to make a case for historically Black colleges and universities. He cited his role as an HBCU Week ambassador and the chance to speak to someone with power to help. He said the evening ran four hours and 20 minutes.

Smith told CNN he told Trump that firms feared giving to those schools because of his stance on diversity, equity and inclusion. He said Trump agreed to look into it, but had made no firm pledge. Smith also said he had pressed for proof of Trump’s upbeat view of the economy.

On October 21, the show played Smith’s answer. Charlamagne said he would have wanted a sit-down that the public could see. He would have sought an interview, not a private dinner chat. He said he wasn’t holding Smith to a higher standard than anyone else. But he noted that elected leaders had to speak to Trump.

item.title: Anele Tembe Inquest Hears No Clear Signs Of Strangulation
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Anele Tembe's inquest heard that neck injuries did not establish strangulation, while the cause of those marks remained unclear.
item.content:encoded:
Anele Tembe’s neck injuries did not give a pathologist clear proof that she had been strangled before her fatal fall, the expert told the inquest into the death of AKA‘s fiancee.

The evidence addressed a key question in the Cape Town case: whether marks on Tembe’s body showed that someone had hurt her before she went over the hotel balcony. The prosecutor asked the expert if she could tell those wounds apart from injuries caused by the fall.

Tembe, 22, died after falling from the 10th floor of the Pepperclub Hotel on April 11, 2021. She had been staying there with AKA. The inquest is examining what happened and whether the evidence points to anyone being responsible.

The pathologist described two areas of bleeding around Tembe’s neck during testimony on Tuesday. She said friction, pressure or suction could account for the marks, but she could not pin down a cause, Daily Maverick reported.

“I cannot unequivocally say what those wounds were caused by,” she told the court.

She explained that wounds caused just before death could look the same as those suffered in the fall. She also raised the possibility that some injuries happened as Tembe fell. Tree branches and leaves found on her body and in her hair supported possible contact with a tree during the descent.

The expert explained that a neck exam looks for signs of pressure, including bruises that could match fingertips and bleeding in the neck muscles. It did not reveal fractures in the small bone beneath the jaw or the neck cartilage, TimesLIVE reported. The expert said it had not established clear evidence of strangulation. The cause of the marks remained unclear. Her evidence was not a ruling that an assault had, or had not, taken place, and did not establish how Tembe came to fall.

The distinction matters after earlier testimony about fresh scratches and bruises on AKA. A doctor who examined him after Tembe’s death described marks on his arm, leg, knee and neck, but said he could not get a clear account of how they happened.

AKA’s father, Tony Forbes, had also challenged an earlier description of scratches on his son’s back, saying it did not match the medical report.

The court had also heard from a forensic analyst who studied the fall itself. He said the physical evidence could fit a jump or a push, but his work did not determine which had happened. He found that a slip and fall did not fit the physical evidence.

The inquest is due to resume on November 17.

item.title: Rapper Shockingly Asks Judge For Death Sentence & Rejects Further Plea To Spare Him
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Ace NH asked a judge for a death sentence and said he wanted no further plea to spare his life at his December hearing.
item.content:encoded:
Tampa rapper Ace NH asked a judge to sentence him to death and said he did not want his lawyers to make another plea to spare his life at his next hearing, even after his family testified on his behalf.

The rapper, whose legal name is Billy Adams III, made his plea in a handwritten letter shown in a new FOX 13 report. He wanted Judge Mark Wolfe to sentence him to death, as jurors had urged, for killing his girlfriend Alana Sims’ unborn child.

Judge Wolfe, not the jury, has the final say on the sentence. FOX 13 reported that it was unclear whether he would let Ace NH give up the chance to offer more evidence in his favor.

“I don’t want my lawyers to present any mitigation or arguments at this hearing,” Ace NH wrote.

The letter carried an October 12 filing stamp and referred to a hearing set for December 1. At that hearing, both sides can offer final evidence before the judge decides the sentence. Mitigation is the defense’s case for a lesser punishment, which can include testimony about the defendant’s background and family.

Ace NH wrote that his lawyers had explained what giving up that opportunity would mean. He said the choice was his and asked them to respect it.

“I don’t have an issue with the death penalty,” he wrote.

The jury split on how he should be punished. After finding him guilty on September 1, jurors called for life without parole for Sims’ murder. They voted 8-4 for death on the separate charge of killing her unborn child by injury to the mother.

During the penalty phase, his stepmother and two younger brothers told jurors about their bonds with him.

The defense urged jurors to choose life without parole rather than death. Those earlier efforts still mattered: FOX 13 reported that Judge Wolfe would have to consider the evidence already presented to spare his life.

Sims was 22 and five months pregnant when she was shot in New Tampa on January 30, 2023. Her young son was found unharmed in her car near the shooting scene.

Prosecutors argued that Ace NH lured Sims there because he wanted to continue a relationship with another woman. They said he believed he was the unborn child’s father, though he later turned out not to be. His lawyers denied he thought the child was his. They argued that the state had not proved he killed Sims because she was pregnant.

The shooting came three days after his acquittal in a separate double-murder case. In that trial, Ace NH testified that he shot two men at a recording studio in self-defense. Police arrested him in Sims’ case on February 8, 2023.

His next hearing is scheduled for December 1.

item.title: IAMDDB Seeks Advice After Israel Steals Her Image & Denies It
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: IAMDDB said she sought advice after an AI rap video shared by Israel's official accounts sparked a dispute over her likeness.
item.content:encoded:
IAMDDB said she was seeking advice to protect her image after an AI rap video shared by Israel’s official social accounts featured a woman who resembled her. She denied having any part in the clip or its message.

In a statement posted October 20, the Manchester-raised rapper and singer also said her past performance in Israel should not be taken as support for the government’s actions.

The dispute began with a video posted last week, not a new song or performance by IAMDDB. Titled “Jews from Judea (We DID),” it showed an AI-made performer rapping in front of a crowd. Its lyrics defended Jewish historical ties to the region in response to claims of colonialism.

The caption answered “GO BACK WHERE YOU CAME FROM!” with “We did.” Israel’s accounts later removed the clip, but no reason for that decision has been established.

New York-based activist Rafael Shimunov drew attention to a photo of IAMDDB that he said explained the resemblance. Photographer Jackson Bowley took the image for a Crack magazine profile published January 8, 2018, more than eight years before the video appeared.

The likeness claim wasn’t based on the woman’s face alone. Mixmag’s side-by-side comparison showed IAMDDB with braids, a black cropped top and branded trousers. The AI performer appeared in a similar outfit, down to altered versions of the logos. BALR. and Calvin Klein became “RALA.” and “Calvin Kale.”

Shimunov alleged that the photo had been fed into an AI system. The comparison did not establish that, and the video’s creator denied that he had set out to copy IAMDDB.

International Business Times reported that director Eyal Ben Moshe, known as Eyal Be, said he had not known who she was. He also said he could not identify which photographs the AI system might have drawn on.

IAMDDB first challenged the post on October 16, asking why her identity had been used for something she had not agreed to.

Her fuller response addressed her own earlier Israel show. She said former management arranged it when she was a young artist eager to travel, before she understood the situation as she does now. She said she would have made a different choice.

She voiced support for Palestinian people and opposed the killing and suffering of civilians. She also rejected the use of AI to make artists appear involved in messages they had never agreed to share.

“I am taking advice and exploring the appropriate steps to protect my image, my work and my rights,” she said.

item.title: Kid Cudi To Play Jean-Michel Basquiat In His Own Film “Jean”
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Kid Cudi announced "Jean," a film he wrote and plans to direct and star in as Jean-Michel Basquiat, with filming planned for 2027.
item.content:encoded:
Kid Cudi announced “Jean,” a film he wrote about Jean-Michel Basquiat and plans to direct and star in. He said he planned to start filming in 2027.

The rapper shared the news on October 21, along with an early wardrobe test. He said people had asked him for years about playing the New York artist, but none of those projects had come together. This year, he wrote one himself.

Cudi said he read books and spoke with people who knew Basquiat to prepare the script. He also cautioned that the wig in his test was a rough version, not the final look.

Cudi’s plan would add to a screen history that includes Julian Schnabel’s 1996 feature “Basquiat,” with Jeffrey Wright in the lead and David Bowie among its cast. The estate described that film as a mix of fact and fiction about Basquiat’s rise in New York’s art world.

Basquiat’s screen history also includes a role of his own. He appeared as himself in “Downtown 81,” which followed the young artist through Lower Manhattan and its art and music scene. Edo Bertoglio directed the film from a script by Glenn O’Brien.

It was filmed in 1981 but did not reach release until 2000, according to the artist’s estate.

The new role brings a real-life subject to Cudi’s run behind the camera. He unveiled his first film as a director, “Doe,” earlier this year. That project was announced as a drama about addiction and survival, with a cast that included Mark Webber, Leah McNamara, Brandon Scott and Brandon Perea.

He followed that announcement with “Wrong Number,” a horror film from his own script that cast him opposite Barbie Ferreira. Its story follows a self-help author whose new romance leads to stalking and a string of murders. “Jean” gives him a different task: writing for the screen about a person whose life has already been told on film.

Cudi’s “Jean” is also separate from the Basquiat documentary Netflix announced for 2026. Directed by Quinn Whitney Wilson and Viridiana Lieberman, that project drew on rare images, art and memories from friends and family. His sisters helped tell that story, which looked at his life through the eyes of those close to him.

Cudi described the role as an honor, citing the influence Basquiat had on his own work throughout his career. For his own film, Cudi made his aim clear: “This film will be a love letter to Jean, the 80s and NY city.”

item.title: TT Torrez Accuses Funkmaster Flex Of Assaulting Her During Madison Square Garden Confrontation
item.dc:creator: Houston Williams
item.description: TT Torrez leveled serious accusations against Funkmaster Flex after the Knicks lost at Madison Square Garden.
item.content:encoded:
TT Torrez accused Funkmaster Flex of violently shoving her during a confrontation at Madison Square Garden in New York on Tuesday night (October 20) following an argument involving her husband, music executive Shadow Stokes.

The confrontation unfolded during the Philadelphia 76ers’ season opener against the New York Knicks at Madison Square Garden on Tuesday night (October 20). The highly anticipated matchup ended with Philadelphia defeating New York 106-100, but the action on the basketball court was not the only source of tension inside the arena. Away from the game, inside the exclusive Delta Lounge, an argument involving two recognizable figures in New York Hip-Hop radio reportedly escalated into the confrontation that has since attracted widespread attention online.

The explosive allegation emerged in a statement issued by Torrez’s representative at Now PR Agency.

According to the statement, Torrez and Stokes were enjoying an evening together when a verbal disagreement between her husband and Flex escalated into a physical altercation.

The representative alleged that Flex shoved Torrez during the encounter, turning an otherwise pleasant outing into a distressing experience.

“There is no justification for a man to put his hands on a woman, under any circumstances,” the statement declared.

The allegations introduce a troubling dimension to a confrontation that has already attracted attention through video footage circulating on social media.

However, Torrez’s representative insisted the footage provides an incomplete account of what happened.

“The brief video circulating online does not tell the full story. What the public saw was a husband defending his wife.”

Video circulating online shows Stokes moving aggressively toward Flex as bystanders watch the confrontation unfold. Multiple security guards eventually restrain Stokes as tensions escalate inside the arena.

However, the footage does not establish what happened immediately before the confrontation or independently confirm allegations that Flex physically assaulted Torrez.

Flex wasted little time responding to speculation that he had been punched.

“HAHAHAHAHA! PLEASE! YOU WISH I GOT PUNCHED IN THE FACE!” Flex wrote on social media alongside a screenshot of a TMZ editor requesting comment. “I GUESS I GOT THESE LABEL GUYS KINDA ANGRY! THEY WANNA SUE WHEN THEY DONT GET THEY WAY!”

The statement also revealed allegations of a longstanding professional conflict between Torrez and Flex, two prominent personalities associated with HOT 97.

Torrez endured years of alleged harassment, intimidation and bullying involving her former colleague, according to her representative.

Torrez reportedly pursued professional and legal remedies instead of publicly addressing those grievances.

The representative claimed those efforts resulted in a settlement with MediaCo HOT 97 and a nondisparagement agreement.

The statement further accused Flex of continuing to violate that agreement.

Her representative Roseay Met said she intends to continue addressing the situation through legal counsel rather than engaging in public arguments.

No criminal charges have been announced by law enforcement.

or additional legal proceedings stemming from the alleged confrontation were identified in the statement.

AllHipHop has messaged Funkmaster Flex for comment.

item.title: Nicki Minaj Promises Fans Cash For Watch-Party Fashion Contest
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Nicki Minaj promised fans cash for their "Million Dollar Pitch Competition" fashion posts and asked the Barbz to help pick winners.
item.content:encoded:
Nicki Minaj promised cash for fans’ fashion posts tied to her “Million Dollar Pitch Competition” watch party. The Barbz had their own prize contest as the show hit streaming.

The rapper named her first four winners on X on Tuesday night. She said more people had made the cut and asked fans to help choose the rest through polls.

“These are my first 4,” she wrote as she shared the first batch of entries. She planned to let the Barbz decide who else would get a prize.

Her next posts split the field by style. One round focused on evening gowns, with three entries she labeled “Champagne glass,” “Pink carpet” and “Money chest.” She said that group would have just one winner.

She also put four more fans in a “PRETTY IN PANTS” group and told her followers she would post a poll for that round, too. Each post carried the #MillionDollarPitch and #MillionDollarFit tags.

The fan contest came as Minaj’s work as a judge reached viewers on Prime Video and YouTube. The Small Business Administration’s special paired her with Grant Cardone and Airbnb co-founder Joe Gebbia. Dean Cain served as host, and President Donald Trump also appeared. Minaj had discussed her judging role on Fox News in September.

The SBA contest’s $1 million prize pool came from Clover Network. Five small-business finalists competed for shares of the money, with $400,000 set aside for first place. Minaj’s posts about the Barbz promised “a few dollars” but did not name a cash amount for her fan prizes.

The contest was taped in Washington on September 18 before its October 20 streaming debut. Minaj kept the premiere going on X with both the fashion posts and a fresh show of support for Trump.

“Not going anywhere. Right where I need to be,” she wrote in response to a fan’s post about Trump calling her his favorite.

Her stance followed her September appearance on “The Ingraham Angle” with SBA chief Kelly Loeffler to discuss the show. During that chat, Minaj said she would not make excuses for her support of the president.

For the fans picked in her first round, she closed with a promise and a joke: “You’ll be sent a few dollars. Don’t spend it all in one place.”

item.title: Anuel AA Barely Listens To Trap Now As Corridos Shape His Next Move
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Anuel AA opened up about his shift toward corridos and the family time behind his four-year wait to release a new album.
item.content:encoded:
Anuel AA said corridos had all but pushed trap and reggaeton out of his own playlist. Yet he still planned a return to the sounds that made him a star.

He shared plans for a full corridos album at Billboard Latin Music Week in Miami Beach. He said he had spent more of this year in Mexico than in the United States, EFE reported. He had also filled his time in the car with corridos. To him, their rise had brought a new style the music world needed.

He named Peso Pluma, Fuerza Regida, Tito Double P and Neton Vega among the acts he admired. They were friends, but he was also a fan of their work.

Part of the draw was how they sang. He praised their skill and the way many of them worked without Auto-Tune. He also felt the music shared some of trap’s street roots, though each style took its own approach. He called the full corridos set a gift for Mexico.

Yet his next move would still leave room for both sounds. His other planned album, “Real Hasta La Muerte 2,” would blend trap and reggaeton and build on his 2018 debut.

That interest had already led him to work with stars from the genre. In July, he joined Luis R Conriquez and Fuerza Regida on “Hay Con Que,” from Conriquez’s “Muchacho Alegre.” The official lyric video came out ahead of the album’s July 10 release.

He linked the four-year wait since “LLNM2” to a wish to live more fully. During the Billboard chat, he spoke about the time he wanted with his loved ones.

“I wanted to spend more time with my children and my family,” he said.

He had kept working while making room for that time. His most recent single, “Vuelve,” arrived on October 9.

He also shared “Los Veo,” a track from the corridos set made with producer Alex Torres. He linked that project to time spent in Mexico through some of his low points.

Anuel hoped to put both albums out together. He did not set a date, though he said he would celebrate the project on his November 26 birthday.

item.title: Funkmaster Flex Breaks Silence After All Hell Breaks Loose At Knicks Game
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Funkmaster Flex named Shadow Stokes after a Knicks game scuffle, denied taking a punch and promised more of his account Thursday.
item.content:encoded:
Funkmaster Flex pushed back on claims that he was punched during a Knicks game scuffle, naming Shadow Stokes in two posts about the encounter.

The Hot 97 DJ posted a clip of the clash in a crowded hall. He then came back with a blunt response. “SHADOW STOKES COULD NEVER PUNCH ME!” he wrote.

The clip showed a group of men pressed together near a door. Arms stretched across the group, with hands on shoulders and backs. The camera then swung away from that group toward more people farther down the hall. Some stood and watched as the crowd moved past them.

The brief, partly blocked view did not show who started the clash. It also did not give AllHipHop a clear view of who struck whom. Flex, for his part, denied that he took a punch to the face.

View this post on Instagram

His first post paired a string of laughing emojis with questions about the clash. Flex asked when he had been assaulted and said he was minding his business. He then turned to someone he called Shadow and asked who had been with him. He did not name that other person.

In the next post, Flex used Stokes’ full name. He also placed his own words over the clip to push back on the punch claim. His message mocked that account of the clash rather than laying out how it began.

Stokes was not a new name in Flex’s world. The two had worked on the same record years before this clash. Credits for Flex’s 2005 “Carshow Tour CD & DVD” listed Stokes as a co-executive producer for Casino Entertainment. Flex was among the project’s executive producers. Koch Records put out the set more than two decades ago.

Stokes also worked on the label side. In a 2010 AllHipHop interview, DJ Kay Slay named him among E1’s radio staff as he discussed the team working his records. Flex did not say how his ties to Stokes reached this point.

The Knicks hosted the Philadelphia 76ers at Madison Square Garden on Tuesday, October 20. Flex posted his latest response the next morning.

View this post on Instagram

He ended that post by promising more of his account Thursday at 7 p.m.: “I GOT A STORY TO TELL!”

item.title: LeBron James Gets Chippy, Cusses Out Heckling Knicks Fans At 76ers Debut
item.dc:creator: Chuck Creekmur (@ChuckCreekmur)
item.description: LeBron James got an earful from New York Knicks fans during his Philadelphia 76ers debut, but the NBA legend gave them a mouthful before he left Madison Square Garden. First of all, he walked away with a victory. Watch this though! The 41-year-old superstar and the Sixers opened his record 24th NBA season Tuesday night …
item.content:encoded:
LeBron James got an earful from New York Knicks fans during his Philadelphia 76ers debut, but the NBA legend gave them a mouthful before he left Madison Square Garden.

First of all, he walked away with a victory.

Watch this though!

The 41-year-old superstar and the Sixers opened his record 24th NBA season Tuesday night with a 106-100 win over the defending champion Knicks, whose fans apparently had some unfinished business with King James. He even has a special pin with “24” on it.

As LeBron approached the free throw line, the Garden erupted with a rather unwelcoming message.

“We don’t want you! We don’t want you!”

Now, that’s some New York hospitality!

James and his agent, Rich Paul, at one point indicated that New York would have been his preferred free agency destination if the Knicks hadn’t captured the chip. That was their first NBA championship since 1973, the year Hip-Hop was “born.” That is a long time!

Instead, LeBron landed in Philadelphia, where the Sixers have assembled a formidable collection of talent in pursuit of their first championship since 1983.

The Knicks might want to reconsider those chants. There was more, as seen above in the video.

James finished with 14 points and nine rebounds while Tyrese Maxey contributed 28 points. Jaylen Brown added 19, and Joel Embiid recorded 13 points and 11 rebounds. Great showing of force!

The Sixers also displayed some promising chemistry, which has not manifested fully yet. They had a nice 11-0 third quarter run.

“We did that on the fly,” James said…and with the Eagles not flying, Philly kinda needs this energy from the Sixers.

Y’all know it’s wild when Spike Lee attempts to calm a situation. Imagine Spike Lee negotiating a Knicks ceasefire during opening night!? Wild night!

Big Bron did nothing to diminish the significance of New York’s championship celebration.

“I wouldn’t say that,” James said. “It was a great night for New York fans. Fifty-plus years. I was a part of that at one point where we hadn’t won a major championship in Cleveland in over 50 years. The fans will never forget this moment.”

The biggest question is whether James, Embiid, Brown and Maxey can translate their impressive individual résumés into a championship. That is truly all that matters and they have two years to accomplish it.

For now, LeBron has one victory, Knicks fans have their banner, and the Eastern Conference has a fascinating new rivalry.

We gon’ see!
